description: Weighted A* is A* that trusts its heuristic more. It expands the open state with the lowest `g + w · h`, where the weight `w` is at least 1. A larger `w` pushes the search toward the goal, so it usually expands far fewer states. The price is quality: with an *admissible* heuristic (one that never overestimates), the path costs at most `w` times the optimum (*bounded-suboptimal*). With `w = 1` it is plain A*. The heuristic-search crate takes `w` as a fraction `p/q` and orders by `q · g + p · h`, so integer costs stay exact.

papers.title: Heuristic search viewed as path finding in a graph
